title: Limiting optimized QAOA energy in the SK model
formal: Determine \(A=\sup _{p\ge 1} \sup _{\gamma ,\beta \in \mathbb{R} ^{p}} a_{p}(\gamma ,\beta )\), where \(a_{p}(\gamma ,\beta )=\lim _{n\to \infty} n^{- 1} E_{J}[\langle \psi _{p,J}(\gamma ,\beta )|H_{J}|\psi _{p,J}(\gamma ,\beta )\rangle ]\) for the Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick Hamiltonian and QAOA state defined below. The benchmark requires absolute error at most \(1/100\) in energy per spin.

context:
QAOA alternates evolution under an objective Hamiltonian and a simple mixing Hamiltonian. Here its optimized energy is measured on a standard random spin-glass ensemble after the number of spins tends to infinity.

Theorem 1 identifies this fixed-depth ensemble performance with the high-degree limit of the normalized MaxCut performance on large-girth regular graphs. This supplies a precise model for the original MaxCut question without assuming an interchange of limits.

Section 5 conjectures that the limiting optimized performance equals \(\Pi\)*, approximately 0.763166 in the source normalization. Asking for A with the benchmark numerical tolerance is a quantitative reformulation and is not logically equivalent to exact equality.

Letting depth grow on one fixed finite instance before taking the size limit gives a different question. The retained target fixes the ensemble-limit-first convention.
why: The limiting optimized energy of QAOA asks whether a central quantum optimization ansatz can reach the statistical-mechanics optimum after taking the infinite-instance limit.
status_note: The source conjectures the exact limiting optimum. The retained numerical task keeps its ensemble-limit-first convention; no rigorous determination within 0.01 was located.

progress.text: The source proves the fixed-depth SK/large-girth MaxCut equivalence and states the limiting Parisi-value conjecture in Section 5.

sentences: QAOA is a widely studied quantum optimization ansatz using alternating objective and mixing operations.
The SK model provides a canonical random quadratic objective with a known limiting optimum.
The question asks for the best limiting energy reachable by finite-depth QAOA when depth is subsequently allowed to grow.
Angles are optimized only after taking the infinite-size ensemble limit.
The source conjectures that this limiting value reaches the Parisi optimum, and the card now accepts a proved numerical determination within 0.01.

definitions: For \(n\ge 2\) let \(J_{ij}, 1\le i<j\le n\), be independent real normal random variables of mean 0 and variance 1. On \((\mathbb{C} ^{2})^{\otimes n}\), let \(Z_{i}\) and \(X_{i}\) act on the i-th qubit by the Pauli matrices \(Z=diag(1,- 1)\) and X with off-diagonal entries 1 and diagonal entries 0. Put \(H_{J}=n^{- 1/2}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}Z_{i} Z_{j}\) and \(B_{n}=\sum_{i} X_{i}\). Let |+⟩=\((|0\rangle +|1\rangle )/\sqrt{2}\). For integer depth \(p\ge 1\) and fixed real angle vectors \(\gamma ,\beta \in \mathbb{R} ^{p}\), define |\(\psi _{p,J}\rangle =e^{- i\beta _{p} B_{n}}e^{- i\gamma _{p} H_{J}}\cdots e^{- i\beta _{1} B_{n}}e^{- i\gamma _{1} H_{J}}|+\rangle ^{\otimes n}\). Matrix exponentials have their usual convergent-series meaning; states have unit norm. Expectation is over J. The n limit exists for each fixed p and angles as established for this model in the source. Angles may depend on p but are fixed independently of n and J. First take the infinite-n ensemble limit for fixed angles, then optimize those angles, then take the supremum over finite depths. Supremum need not be attained. Identity layers imply that the optimized depth values are nondecreasing. They are bounded by \(\Pi *=\lim _{n\to \infty} E_{J}[\max _{z\in \{- 1,1\}^{n}} n^{- 1/2}\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}z_{i} z_{j}]/n\), the finite Parisi ground-state value in this normalization. Maximization, rather than minimization, fixes the sign convention.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguous value a and a Lean proof that |\(a- A|\le 1/100\), or certified lower and upper bounds of width at most \(1/50\) with the midpoint as answer. Exact determination also qualifies. Merely restating the defining supremum, reporting floating-point optimization at finitely many depths, or interchanging depth and instance-size limits is insufficient. Equality with \(\Pi\)* is a stronger possible answer, not assumed by the target.
